summary.text: Vince Fong is the Republican incumbent for California's 20th District, a Bakersfield native who worked for Reps. Bill Thomas and Kevin McCarthy before serving in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2024. He won a May 2024 special election to succeed McCarthy and a full term that November, and advanced from the June 2026 primary.

paragraphs.text: Fong was born in Bakersfield in 1979. Wikipedia reports that his parents were Chinese immigrants and that he attended West High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from UCLA in 2001 and a master's degree in public administration from Princeton University in 2003.

According to his official biography, he began his career with Rep. Bill Thomas, then chair of the House Ways and Means Committee, working on international trade policy. After returning to Kern County, he spent nearly a decade as district director to Kevin McCarthy, then House Majority Leader.

His official biography says he helped organize a Valley Fever Symposium to draw national attention to the disease. Wikipedia lists his service on the boards of Goodwill Industries of South Central California, the Jim Burke Education Foundation and Honor Flight Kern County.

Fong was elected to the California State Assembly in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, 2020 and 2022, representing Bakersfield-area districts. His official biography says he worked in Sacramento on energy, transportation, infrastructure and supply chains, and the bills he authored included measures on catalytic converter theft and wildfire prevention through controlled grazing. He resigned his Assembly seat on May 24, 2024.

McCarthy resigned from Congress effective December 31, 2023, and Fong ran in the special election to succeed him. He advanced to a runoff against Tulare County Sheriff Mike Boudreaux and won the May 21, 2024 runoff, 60.6 percent to 39.4 percent. He was sworn in on June 3, 2024, and won a full term in November 2024 with 65.1 percent of the vote.

In Congress he serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure, Science, Space, and Technology, and Homeland Security committees, and he belongs to the Republican Study Committee, Western Caucus and Congressional Valley Fever Task Force, among other caucuses.
Fong advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary with 68.2 percent of the vote. He is a lifelong Kern County resident and lives in Bakersfield with his wife, Amanda.
